title: Introduction to Digital Logic Laboratory
description: Introduction to common digital integrated circuits: gates, memory circuits, MSI components. Operating characteristics, specifications, applications. Design of simple combinational and sequential digital systems (arithmetic processors game-playing machines). Construction and debugging techniques using hardware description languages and CAD tools.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 31 and ( EECS 10 or EECS 12 or I&C SCI 32 )

title: Object-Oriented Systems and Programming
description: Primitive types and expressions. The class and method definition. Information hiding and encapsulation. Objects and reference. Overloading. Constructors. Inheritance basics. Programming with inheritance. Dynamic binding and polymorphism. Exception handling. An overview of streams and file input/output. Programming laboratory.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 22L

title: Discrete-Time Signals and Systems
description: Analysis of discrete-time linear-time-invariant (DTLTI) systems in the time domain and using z-transforms. Introduction to techniques based on Discrete-Time, Discrete, and Fast Fourier Transforms. Examples of their application to digital signal processing and digital communications.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 70A

title: Engineering Probability
description: Sets and set operations; nature of probability, sample spaces, fields of events, probability measures; conditional probability, independence, random variables, distribution functions, density functions, conditional distributions and densities; moments, characteristic functions, random sequences, independent and Markov sequences.
prerequisites_raw: MATH 2D

title: Network Analysis I
description: Modeling and analysis of electrical networks. Basic network theorems. Sinusoidal steady state and transient analysis of RLC networks and the impedance concept.
prerequisites_raw: PHYSICS 7D and ( EECS 10 or EECS 12 or ENGRMAE 10 or I&C SCI 31 or ENGRCEE 20 )

title: Network Analysis II
description: Laplace transforms, complex frequency, and the s-plane. Network functions and frequency response, including resonance. Bode plots. Two-port network characterization.
prerequisites_raw: ( BME 60B or EECS 10 or EECS 12 or I&C SCI 31 or ENGRCEE 20 or ENGRMAE 10 ) and EECS 70A

title: Network Analysis I Laboratory
description: Laboratory to accompany EECS 70A .
prerequisites_raw: PHYSICS 7D and ( EECS 10 or EECS 12 or BME 60B or ENGRCEE 20 or ENGRMAE 10 )

title: Network Analysis II Laboratory
description: Laboratory to accompany EECS 70B . Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ( BME 60B or EECS 10 or EECS 12 or I&C SCI 31 or ENGRCEE 20 or ENGRMAE 10 ) and EECS 70A

title: Introduction to Machine Vision
description: The use of digital computers for the analysis of visual scenes; image formation and sensing, color, segmentation, shape estimation, motion, stereo, pattern classification, computer architectures, applications. Computer experiments are used to illustrate fundamental principles.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 150 or EECS 50

title: System Software
description: Multiprogramming, interrupt, processes, kernel, parallelism, critical sections, deadlocks, communication, multiprocessing, multilevel memory management, binding, name management, file systems, protection, resource allocation, scheduling. Experience with concurrent programming, synchronization mechanisms, interprocess communication.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 112 and ( I&C SCI 46 or EECS 114 )

title: Organization of Digital Computers
description: Building blocks and organization of digital computers, the arithmetic, control, and memory units, and input/out devices and interfaces. Microprogramming and microprocessors.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 31L

title: Organization of Digital Computers Laboratory
description: Specification and implementation of a processor-based system using a hardware description language such as VHDL. Hands-on experience with design tools including simulation, synthesis, and evaluation using testbenches.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 112

title: Processor Hardware/Software Interfaces
description: Hardware/software interfacing, including memory and bus interfaces, devices, I/O, and compiler code generation/instruction scheduling. Experience microcontroller programming and interfacing. Specific compiler code generation techniques including local variable and register allocations, instruction dependence and scheduling, and code optimization.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 112

title: Engineering Data Structures and Algorithms
description: Introduces abstract behavior of classes data structures, alternative implementations, informal analysis of time and space efficiency. Also introduces classic algorithms and efficient algorithm design techniques (recursion, divide-and-conquer, branch-and-bound, dynamic programming).
prerequisites_raw: EECS 40

title: Introduction to Data Management
description: Introduction to the design of databases and the use of database management systems (DBMS) for applications. Topics include entity-relationship modeling for design, relational data model, relational algebra, relational design theory, and Structured Query Language (SQL) programming.
prerequisites_raw: I&C SCI 33 with a minimum grade of C or EECS 114

title: Parallel Computer Systems
description: General introduction to parallel computing focusing on parallel algorithms and architectures. Parallel models: Flynn's taxonomy, dataflow models. Parallel architectures: systolic arrays, hypercube architecture, shared memory machines, dataflow machines, reconfigurable architectures. Parallel algorithms appropriate to each machine type area also discussed.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 20 and EECS 114 and EECS 112

title: Data and Knowledge Science and Engineering
description: Introduction of basic concepts in artificial intelligence. Knowledge representation and reasoning, search, planning, declarative programing, problem solving, and data science.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 114

title: VLSI
description: Design techniques for Very Large Scale Integrated (VLSI) systems and chips. Review CMOS and related process technologies; primitives such as logic gates and larger design blocks; layout; floor planning; design hierarchy, component interfaces; use of associated CAD tools for design.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 112 and EECS 170B

title: Fundamentals of Parallel Computing
description: Fundamentals of parallel computing, focusing on parallel algorithms and architectures. Topics include design of parallel and I/O efficient algorithms, basics of parallel machine architectures, and current/emerging programming models (shared memory, distributed memory, and accelerators).
prerequisites_raw: ( EECS 12 or COMPSCI 152 ) and EECS 114

title: System Security
description: Fundamentals and practices of system security. Topics include cryptographic (encryption, decryption, and message authentication), software vulnerabilities (buffer overflow), network security (layer 2-7 attacks and defenses and PKI), web security (XSS and XSRF), and privacy.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 22 or I&C SCI 45C

title: Introduction to Machine Learning for Engineers
description: Introduction to ML with a special focus on engineering applications. Starts with a mathematical background required for ML and covers various models for supervised learning (classification and regression) and unsupervised learning (clustering).
prerequisites_raw: EECS 55 and EECS 145 and EECS 12 . Recommended: EECS 114

title: Quantum Information and Architecture
description: Fundamentals of quantum mechanics and quantum information; learn the principles, advantages, and challenges of quantum computing and its architectures; acquire hands-on experience with basic quantum information techniques.
prerequisites_raw: MATH 3A and ( EECS 145 or PHYSICS 50 )

title: Communication Systems I
description: Introduction to analog communication systems including effects of noise. Modulation-demodulation for AM, DSB-SC, SSB, VSB, QAM, FM, PM, and PCM with application to radio, television, and telephony. Signal processing as applied to communication systems.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 55 and EECS 150

title: Communication Systems II
description: Signal space analysis. Optimum receivers for digital communication. Maximum a posteriori and maximum likelihood detection. Matched filter and correlation receiver. PAM, QAM, PSK, FSK, and MSK and their performance. Introduction to equalization, synchronization, information theory, and error control codes.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 141A

title: Antenna Design for Wireless Communication Links
description: Analysis and synthesis of antennas and antenna arrays. Adaptive arrays and digital beam forming for advanced wireless links. Friis transmission formula. Wireless communication equations for cell-site and mobile antennas, interference, slow and fast fading in mobile communication.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 180A

title: Electrical Engineering Analysis
description: Vector calculus, complex functions, and linear algebra with applications to electrical engineering problems.
prerequisites_raw: MATH 3D

title: Computer Networks
description: Computer network architectures, protocols, and applications. Internet congestion control, addressing, and routing. Local area networks. Multimedia networking.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 55 or STATS 67

title: Continuous-Time Signals and Systems
description: Characteristics and properties of continuous-time (analog) signals and systems. Analysis of linear time-invariant continuous-time systems using differential equation convolutional models. Analysis of these systems using Laplace transforms, Fourier series, and Fourier transforms. Examples from applications to telecommunications.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 70A and MATH 3D

title: Digital Signal Processing
description: Nature of sampled data, sampling theorem, difference equations, data holds, z-transform, w-transform, digital filters, Butterworth and Chebychev filters, quantization effects.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 50

title: Digital Signal Processing Design and Laboratory
description: Design and implementation of algorithms on a DSP processor and using computer simulation. Applications in signal and image processing, communications, radar, etc.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 152A

title: Senior Design Project I
description: Teaches problem definition, detailed design, integration, and testability with teams of students specifying, designing, building, and testing complex systems. Lectures include engineering values, discussions, and ethical ramifications of engineering decisions.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 113 or EECS 170C or COMPSCI 145

title: Senior Design Project II
description: Teaches problem definition, detailed design, integration, and testability with teams of students specifying, designing, building, and testing complex systems. Lectures include engineering values, discussions, and ethical ramifications of engineering decisions. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: EECS 159A

title: Introduction to Control Systems
description: Modeling, stability, and specifications of feedback control systems. Root locus, Bode plots, Nyquist criteria, and state-space methods for dynamic analysis and design.
prerequisites_raw: ( EECS 10 or EECS 12 or ENGRMAE 10 or BME 60B or ENGRCEE 20 ) and EECS 150 and EECS 170B and EECS 170LB

title: Control Systems I Laboratory
description: Laboratory accompanying EECS 160A . Materials Fee

title: Power Systems
description: Generation, transmission, and use of electrical energy. Fault calculation, protection, stability, and power flow.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 70B

title: Power Systems Laboratory
description: Experiments and field trips relevant to studies in power systems. Materials Fee

title: Industrial and Power Electronics
description: Power switching devices, pulse width modulation (PWM) methods, switching converter topologies, control, and magnetics. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: EECS 170C and EECS 160A

title: Electronics I
description: The properties of semiconductors, electronic conduction in solids, the physics and operation principles of semiconductor devices such as diodes and transistors, transistor equivalent circuits, and transistor amplifiers.
prerequisites_raw: PHYSICS 7D and EECS 70B

title: Electronics II
description: Design and analysis of single-stage amplifiers, biasing circuits, inverters, logic gates, and memory elements based on CMOS transistors.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 70B and EECS 170A and EECS 170LA

title: Electronics III
description: Principles of operation, design, and utilization of integrated circuit modules, including multi-stage amplifiers, operational amplifiers, and logic circuits.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 170B and EECS 170LB

title: Integrated Electronic Circuit Design
description: Design and fabrication of modern digital integrated circuits. Fabrication of CMOS process, transistor-level design simulation, functional characteristics of basic digital integrated circuits, and different logic families including the static and dynamic logic, layout, and extraction of digital circuits.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 170C and EECS 170LC

title: Analog and Communications IC Design
description: Advanced topics in design of analog and communications integrated circuits. Topics include: implementation of passive components in integrated circuits; overview of frequency response of amplifiers, bandwidth estimation techniques, high-frequency amplifier design; design of radio-frequency oscillators.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 170C

title: Electronics I Laboratory
description: Laboratory accompanying EECS 170A to perform experiments on semiconductor material properties, semiconductor device physics and operation principles, and transistor amplifiers to improve experimental skills and to enhance the understanding of lecture materials.
prerequisites_raw: PHYSICS 7D and EECS 70B

title: Electronics II Laboratory
description: Laboratory accompanying EECS 170B .
prerequisites_raw: EECS 170A and EECS 170LA

title: Electronics III Laboratory
description: Laboratory accompanying EECS 170C to provide hands-on training in design of digital/analog circuits/subsystems. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: EECS 170B and EECS 170LB

title: Semiconductor Devices
description: Metal-semiconductor junctions, diodes, bipolar junction transistors, MOS structures, MOSFETs, CMOS technology, LEDs, and laser diodes.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 170A

title: Fundamentals of Solid-State Electronics and Materials
description: Physical properties of semiconductors and the roles materials play in device operation. Topics include: crystal structure, phonon vibrations, energy band, transport phenomenon, optical properties and quantum confinement effect essential to the understanding of electronic, optoelectronic and nanodevices.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 170A

title: Microelectromechanical Systems (MEMS)
description: Small-scale machines, small-scale phenomena, MEMS fabrication, MEMS CAD tools, MEMS devices and packaging, MEMS testing.

title: Engineering Electromagnetics I
description: Electrostatics, magnetostatics, and electromagnetic fields: solutions to problems in engineering applications; transmission lines, Maxwell's equations and phasors, plane wave propagation, reflection, and transmission.
prerequisites_raw: PHYSICS 7E and EECS 145

title: Engineering Electromagnetics II
description: Time-varying electromagnetic fields, plane waves, polarization, guidance of waves like rectangular waveguides and microstrips, optical fibers resonant cavities, skin effects and losses, spherical waves, radiation and reception of waves, antenna basics.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 180A

title: Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) Analysis and Design
description: Design of microwave amplifiers including low-noise amplifiers, multiple stage amplifiers, power amplifiers, and introduction to broadband amplifiers. The goal is to provide the basic knowledge for the design of microwave amplifiers ranging from wireless system to radar system.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 180A

title: Optical Electronics
description: Photodiodes and optical detection, photometry and radiometry, geometric optics, lens theory, imaging system, EM wave propagation, optical waveguides and fibers, heterojunction structures, laser theory, semiconductor lasers, and optical transmission system.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 180A

title: Special Topics in Electrical and Computer Engineering
description: Studies special topics in selected areas of Electrical and Computer Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science Internship
description: Students majoring in EECS may receive credit for an approved internship, working at a company under the supervision of an industry mentor and a faculty advisor. Enables students to gain valuable experience in a professional setting and enhance their skills.

title: Group Study
description: Group study of selected topics in Electrical and Computer Engineering.

title: Individual Study
description: For undergraduate Engineering majors in supervised but independent reading, research, or design. Students taking Individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.

title: Individual Study
description: For undergraduate Engineering majors in supervised but independent reading, research, or design. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.

title: Techniques in Medical Imaging: X-ray, Nuclear, and NMR Imaging
description: Ionizing radiation, planar and tomographic radiographic and nuclear imaging, magnetism, NMR, MRI imaging.

title: Digital Image Processing
description: Pixel-level digital image representation and elementary operations; Fourier and other unitary transforms; compression, enhancement, filtering, and restoration; laboratory experience is provided.

title: Digital Image Processing
description: Pixel-level digital image representation and elementary operations; Fourier and other unitary transforms; compression, enhancement, filtering, and restoration; laboratory experience is provided.

title: Personalized Medical Devices
description: Introduces students to fundamental aspects of medical devices and discusses therapeutic as well as diagnostic devices. Basic aspects of microfluidics and biology critical to personalized medical systems are studied. Typical FDA approval pathways for medical devices are presented.

title: Advanced System Software
description: Study of operating systems including interprocess communication, scheduling, resource management, concurrency, reliability, validation, protection and security, and distributed computing support. System software design languages and modeling analysis.

title: Advanced System Software
description: Study of operating systems including interprocess communication, scheduling, resource management, concurrency, reliability, validation, protection and security, and distributed computing support. System software design languages and modeling analysis.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: Undergraduate-level knowledge of system software (e.g. EECS 111 ) and organization of digital computers (e.g. UCI EECS 112)

title: Computer Architecture
description: Problems in hardware, firmware (microprogram), and software. Computer architecture for resource sharing, real-time applications, parallelism, microprogramming, and fault tolerance. Various architectures based on cost/performance and current technology.

title: Computer Architecture
description: Problems in hardware, firmware (microprogram), and software. Computer architecture for resource sharing, real-time applications, parallelism, microprogramming, and fault tolerance. Various architectures based on cost/performance and current technology.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: Undergraduate-level knowledge of organization of digital computers (e.g. EECS 112 and EECS 112L )

title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
description: Computer algorithms from a practical standpoint. Algorithms for symbolic and numeric problems such as sorting, searching, graphs, and network flow. Analysis includes algorithm time and space complexity.

title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
description: Computer algorithms from a practical standpoint. Algorithms for symbolic and numeric problems such as sorting, searching, graphs, and network flow. Analysis includes algorithm time and space complexity.

title: Advanced Application of Algorithms
description: Medium-sized group and individual programming project. Topics include specification requirements documentation, practical implementation of algorithms, and testing/verification of design.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: Undergraduate course work in engineering data structures and algorithms

title: VLSI System Design
description: Overview of integrated fabrication, circuit simulation, basic device physics, device layout, timing; MOS logic design; layout generation, module generation, techniques for very large scale integrated circuit design.

title: VLSI System Design
description: Overview of integrated fabrication, circuit simulation, basic device physics, device layout, timing; MOS logic design; layout generation, module generation, techniques for very large scale integrated circuit design.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: Undergraduate-level knowledge of organization of digital computers (e.g. EECS 112 )

title: Advanced Digital Signal Processing Architecture
description: Study the latest DSP architectures for applications in communication (wired and wireless) and multimedia processing. Emphasis given to understanding the current design techniques and to evaluate the performance, power, and application domain of the latest DSP processors.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 213P with a minimum grade of B-

title: Topics in Computer Engineering
description: New research results in computer engineering.

title: Embedded System Modeling
description: Computational models for embedded systems. System-level specification and description languages. Concepts, requirements, examples. Embedded system models at different levels of abstraction. Modeling of test benches, design under test, IP components. Discrete event simulation, semantics, and algorithms. Formerly EECS 222A.

title: Real-Time Computer Systems
description: Time bases, clock synchronization, real-time communication protocols, specification of requirements, task scheduling. Validation of timelines, real-time configuration management.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 211P with a minimum grade of B- and EECS 213P with a minimum grade of B-

title: High-Performance Computing
description: Fundamentals of high-performance computing, covering both theory and practice. Topics include performance analysis and tuning, design of parallel and I/O efficient algorithms, basics of parallel machine architectures, and current/emerging programming models (shared memory, distributed memory, and accelerators).
prerequisites_raw: EECS 215 with a minimum grade of B- or COMPSCI 260 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Embedded System Software
description: Embedded system software concepts, requirements, examples, for engineering applications such as multi-media and automotive. Software generation methodology. Algorithmic specification, design constraints. Embedded operating systems. Static, dynamic, real-time scheduling. Input/output, interrupt handling. Code generation, compilation, instruction set simulation. Formerly EECS 222C.

title: Cyber-Physical System Design
description: Model-based design of cyber-physical systems including, e.g., plant, sensing, control, actuation, embedded hardware/software, communication, real-time analysis, various levels of simulation (MILS, SILS, HILS), tools and methodologies for automatic synthesis, and application from various interdisciplinary domains.

title: Energy Efficiency
description: Green energy sources for production, transmission, storage, and utilization of electricity, with a special focus on solar, wind, and nuclear energy production. Study of newly developed renewable sources of energy including capital cost, product cost, environmental issues, and technical feasibility.

title: Introduction to Machine Learning
description: Introduces fundamental concepts in programming and machine learning. The goal is to provide an accessible introduction to the field of machine learning and related techniques for students with a wide variety of engineering degrees.

title: Advanced System Security
description: Advanced study about system security. Topics include software vulnerabilities (buffer overflow), vulnerability discovery (fuzzing), network security, side-channel analysis (power analysis and micro-architecture attacks), machine-learning security, IoT security, and privacy (differential privacy).

title: Data Privacy
description: Presents data privacy in the digital age from multiple perspectives, including theoretical frameworks for privacy; tracking practices and privacy-enhancing technologies in various application domains; and data protection laws and policy.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: Students should have familiarity with networking (web/HTTP, DNS, mobile devices) ( EECS 148 or equivalent), probability ( EECS 55 or equivalent), and programming in python ( EECS 12 or equivalent) at the undergraduate level

title: Quantum Information and Architecture
description: Fundamentals of quantum mechanics and quantum information; learn the principles, advantages, and challenges of quantum computing and its architectures; acquire hands-on experience with basic quantum information techniques.
prerequisites_raw: Knowledge in linear algebra and complex analysis

title: Random Processes
description: Extensions of probability theory to random variables varying with time. General properties of stochastic processes. Convergence. Estimation, including nonlinear and linear minimum mean square error and maximum likelihood. Spectral density and linear filters. Poisson processes and discrete-time Markov chains.

title: Random Processes
description: Extensions of probability theory to random variables varying with time. General properties of stochastic processes. Convergence. Estimation, including nonlinear and linear minimum mean square error and maximum likelihood. Spectral density and linear filters. Poisson processes and discrete-time Markov chains.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: Knowledge of engineering probability (e.g. EECS 55 )

title: Digital Communications I
description: Concepts and applications of digital communication systems. Baseband digital transmission of binary, multiamplitude, and multidimensional signals. Introduction to and performance analysis of different modulation schemes.

title: Digital Communications I
description: Concepts and applications of digital communication systems. Baseband digital transmission of binary, multiamplitude, and multidimensional signals. Introduction to and performance analysis of different modulation schemes.

title: Digital Communications II
description: Concepts and applications of equalization, multi-carrier modulation, spread spectrum and CDMA. Digital communications through fading memory channels.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 241A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Digital Communications II
description: Concepts and applications of equalization, multi-carrier modulation, spread spectrum, and CDMA. Digital communications through fading memory channels.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 241AP with a minimum grade of B-

title: Information Theory
description: Fundamental capabilities and limitations of information sources and information transmission systems. Analytical framework for modeling and evaluating communication systems: entropy, mutual information asymptotic equipartition property, entropy rates of a stochastic process, data compression, channel capacity, differential entropy, the Gaussian channel.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 240 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Wireless Communications
description: Introduction to wireless communications systems. Wireless channel modeling. Single carries, spread spectrum, and multi-carrier wireless modulation schemes. Diversity techniques. Multiple-access schemes. Transceiver design and system level tradeoffs. Brief overview of GSM, CDMA, (IS-95) and 2.5, 3G cellular schemes.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 241B with a minimum grade of B-

title: Wireless Communications
description: Introduction to wireless communications systems. Wireless channel modeling. Single carries, spread spectrum, and multi-carrier wireless modulation schemes. Diversity techniques. Multiple-access schemes. Transceiver design and system level tradeoffs. Brief overview of GSM, CDMA, (IS-95) and 2.5, 3G cellular schemes.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 241BP with a minimum grade of B-

title: Information Storage
description: Storage architecture, storage network and networking algorithms in data centers, principle of storage devices and non-volatile memory, data consistency, data availability and integrity, power management.

title: Computer and Communication Networks
description: Network architecture of the Internet, telephone networks, cable networks, and cell phone networks. Network performance models. Network performance models. Advanced concepts and implementations of flow and congestion control, addressing, internetworking, forwarding, routing, multiple access, streaming, and quality-of-service.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 148 or COMPSCI 132

title: Digital Signal Processing I
description: Fundamental principles of digital signal processing, sampling, decimation and interpolation, discrete Fourier transforms and FFT algorithms, transversal and recursive filters, discrete random processes, and finite-word effects in digital filters.

title: Digital Signal Processing I
description: Fundamental principles of digital signal processing, sampling, decimation and interpolation, discrete Fourier transforms and FFT algorithms, transversal and recursive filters, discrete random processes, and finite-word effects in digital filters.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: Knowledge of digital signal processing (e.g. EECS 152A )

title: Detection, Estimation, and Demodulation Theory
description: Fundamentals of hypothesis testing and Bayes and Maximum Likelihood Estimation. ARMA and state variable models for random time series analysis. Wiener and Kalman filtering and prediction. Adaptive algorithms for identification and tracking of parameters of time-varying models.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 240 with a minimum grade of B-

title: Machine Learning for Signal Processing
description: Machine learning and computational neuroscience methods for signal processing. Theory and applications are described, as well as practical programming methods in Python using Keras and TensorFlow 2.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: EECS 125 or equivalent undergraduate-level introduction to machine learning and EECS 152A or equivalent undergraduate course in digital signal processing. Knowledge of introductory linear algebra and differential equations, elementary probability theory, and elementary Python programming

title: Unsupervised Computational Neural Networks and Machine Learning
description: Unsupervised machine learning and computational neuroscience methods. Theory and applications are described, as well as practical programming methods in Python using Keras and TensorFlow 2.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: EECS 125 or equivalent undergraduate-level introduction to machine learning. Knowledge of introductory linear algebra and differential equations, elementary probability theory, and elementary Matlab programming

title: Linear Systems I
description: State-space representation of continuous-time and discrete-time linear systems. Controllability, observability, stability. Realization of rational transfer functions.

title: Linear Optimization Methods
description: Formulation, solution, and analysis of linear programming and linear network flow problems. Simplex methods, dual ascent methods, interior point algorithms, and auction algorithms. Duality theory and sensitivity analysis. Shortest path, max-flow, assignment, and minimum cost flow problems.

title: Introduction to Non-Linear Optimization
description: Explores convex optimization problems that arise in scientific and engineering applications, presenting the basic theory, and concentrating on modeling aspects and results useful in applications. Covers the fundamentals of convex optimization and its applications to signal processing, control, machine learning.

title: Industrial and Power Electronics
description: Power switching devices, pulse width modulation (PWM) methods, switching converter topologies, control, and magnetics. Materials Fee

title: Topics in Industrial and Power Electronics
description: Practical design of switching converters, electromagnetic compatibility, thermal management, and/or control methods.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 267A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Advanced Analog Integrated Circuit Design I
description: Basic transistor configurations; differential pairs; active load/current sources; supply/temperature-independent biasing; op-amp gain and output stages; amplifier frequency response and stability compensation; nonidealities in op-amps; noise and dynamic range in analog circuits.

title: Advanced Analog Integrated Circuit Design I
description: Basic transistor configurations; differential pairs; active load/current sources; supply/temperature-independent biasing; op-amp gain and output stages; amplifier frequency response and stability compensation; nonidealities in op-amps; noise and dynamic range in analog circuits.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: Introductory knowledge of control systems (e.g. EECS 160A ) and electronics (e.g. EECS 170C )

title: Advanced Analog Integrated Circuit Design II
description: Advanced transistor modeling issues; discrete-time and continuous-time analog Integrated Circuit (IC) filters; phase-locked loops; design of ICs operating at radio frequencies; low-voltage/low-power design techniques; A/D and D/A converters; AGC circuits.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 270A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Advanced Analog Integrated Circuit Design II
description: Advanced transistor modeling issues; discrete-time and continuous-time analog Integrated Circuit (IC) filters; phase-locked loops; design of ICs operating at radio frequencies; low-voltage/low-power design techniques; A/D and D/A converters; AGC circuits.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 270AP with a minimum grade of B-

title: Design of Integrated Circuits for Broadband Applications
description: Topics include: broadband standards and protocols; high-frequency circuit design techniques; PLL theory and design; design of transceivers; electrical/optical interfaces.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 270A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Radio-Frequency Integrated Circuits and Systems
description: Fundamental topics in radio-frequency (RF) integrated circuits and systems including basic concepts in RF circuits and systems, RF receiver and transmitter architectures, and RF core building blocks such as low-noise amplifiers (LNAs), RF mixers, and power amplifiers.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 270A with a minimum grade of B-

title: MM-Wave and Terahertz Circuits
description: Discussion of the new methodologies, circuits, and systems developed at mm-wave and terahertz frequency ranges due to the growing interest in high speed communication and high frequency signal generation.

title: Radio-Frequency Integrated Circuit Design
description: Topics include RF component modeling; matching network design; transmission line theory/modeling; Smith chart and S-parameters; noise modeling of active and passive components; high-frequency amplifier design; low-noise amplifier (LNA) design; mixer design; RF power amplifier.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 270AP with a minimum grade of B

title: Advanced Semiconductor Devices I
description: Advanced complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (CMOSFET), device scaling, device modeling and fabrication, equivalent circuits, and their applications for digital, analog, RF.

title: Advanced Semiconductor Devices II
description: Metal-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MESFET), heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBT), microwave semiconductor devices, equivalent circuits, device modeling and fabrication, microwave amplifiers, transmitters, and receivers.

title: Nanotechnology
description: Fabrication and characterization techniques of electrical circuit elements at the nanometer scale. Quantized conductance, semiconductor quantum dots, single electron transistors, molecular wires, carbon nanotubes, self-assembly of nano-circuit elements, quantum methods of information processing.

title: Micro-System Design
description: Covers the fundamentals of the many disciplines needed for design of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS): microfabrication technology, structural mechanics on micro-scale, electrostatics, circuit interface, control, computer-aided design, and system integration.

title: Micro-Sensors and Actuators
description: Introduction to the technology of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS). Fundamental principles and applications of important microsensors, actuation principles on microscale. Introduction to the elements of signal processing; processing of materials for micro sensor/actuator fabrication; smart sensors and microsensor/microactuator array devices.

title: Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics I
description: Stationary electromagnetic fields, Maxwell's equations, circuits and transmission lines, plane waves, guided waves, and radiation.

title: Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics II
description: Two- and three-dimensional boundary value problems, dielectric waveguides and other special waveguides, microwave networks and antenna arrays, electromagnetic properties of materials, and electromagnetic optics.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 280A with a minimum grade of B-

title: Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics I
description: Stationary electromagnetic fields, Maxwell's equations, circuits and transmission lines, plane waves, guided waves, and radiation.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: Knowledge of engineering electromagnetics (e.g. EECS 180A )

title: Wireless Communication Links and Antenna Design
description: Provides the fundamental understanding of the electromagnetic part of wireless communication links and their antennas, i.e., their key components. Contains hands-on component where students learn how to use the best CADs used in industry and academia.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: EECS 180A

title: RF Antenna Design
description: Advanced transmission line design, radiation of electromagnetic waves, dipole antennas, antenna arrays, advanced antenna designs, and practical design considerations in communications systems. Course is supplemented by RF design tools and modeling.
prerequisites_raw: EECS 280AP with a minimum grade of B-

title: Optical Communications
description: Introduction to fiber optic communication systems, optical and electro-optic materials, and high-speed optical modulation and switching devices.

title: Nano Imaging
description: Theory and practice of modern nanoscale imaging techniques and applications. Traces the development of microscopy from ancient times to modern day techniques used for visualizing the nano-world from atoms to molecules including hands-on experience in the laboratory.

title: Optical Communications
description: Introduction to fiber optic communication systems, optical and electro-optic materials, and high-speed optical modulation and switching devices.
prerequisites_raw: Undergraduate-level Engineering Electromagnetics I (e.g. EECS E80A)

title: Fabrication of Biomedical and Wearable Microdevices
description: Covers preliminary details on prototyping and fabrication techniques for biomedical and wearable microdevices. Fabrication and behavior of modern biomed device materials such as hydrogel, PDMS, biopolymer, smart materials, and their uses are introduced.
prerequisites_raw: Required: Knowledge of undergraduate-level basic physics

title: Micro/Nano Biotechnology and Biosensing: Fundamentals, Designs, and Applications
description: Provides insight into the current topics in Micro/Nanoscience, Micro/Nanotechnology fundamentals, and their modern-day applications in life sciences. Focus is on Micro/Nanodevices; Sensors’ fundamentals; NanoBioSensors; Microfluidics; Micro/Nanofabrication, detection system-level characterization; performance determination; solid-state materials; and more.

title: Bioinstrumentation
description: Introduces instrumentation used in biomedical research, clinical medicine, and health monitoring. Interfacing of bioelectronics and biomedical sensing are taught with the most updated methods. The integration of bioinstrumentation with data science and cloud computing are introduced.

title: Preparation for M.S. Comprehensive Examination
description: Individual reading and preparation for the M.S. comprehensive examination.

title: Preparation for Ph.D. Preliminary Examination
description: Individual reading and preparation for the Ph.D. preliminary examination.

title: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science Colloquium
description: Invited speakers discuss their latest research results in electrical engineering and computer science.

title: Seminars in Engineering
description: Scheduled each year by individual faculty in major field of interest.

title: Special Topics in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
description: Studies in selected areas of Electrical Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Master of Science Thesis Research
description: Individual research or investigation conducted in the pursuit of preparing and completing the thesis required for the M.S. degree in Engineering.

title: Doctor of Philosophy Dissertation Research
description: Individual research or investigation conducted in preparing and completing the dissertation required for the Ph.D. degree in Engineering.

title: Topics in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
description: Study of Electrical and Computer Engineering concepts.

title: Toxicology and Society
description: Introduces principles of toxicology and societal implications of toxic exposures. Focuses on mechanisms of action, dose-response relationships, exposure pathways, and risk assessment. Includes applications in food safety, occupational health, environmental toxicology, regulatory policy, and health equity.
prerequisites_raw: Recommended: PUBHLTH 1 and PUBHLTH 5

title: Case Studies in Environmental Toxicology
description: Explores toxicology principles through case-based discussions. Topics include exposure routes, absorption, metabolism, and mechanisms of toxicity. Lectures with discussions are delivered by invited faculty experts.
prerequisites_raw: EHS 206B with a minimum grade of B-

title: Principles of Environmental Toxicology
description: Explores molecular, biological, and structure-based toxicity of environmental toxicants. Topics include dose-response relationship, ADME, mechanisms of action, and its impact on the environment, wildlife, and human health. Covered through lectures, research papers, and discussion.

title: Occupational Epidemiology
description: The importance of work environment for workers’ health and productivity has increased with changing technology, work organization, demographics, and occupation/industry structures. This advanced occupational epidemiology course focuses on work environment as exposures, and workers’ health and productivity as outcomes.

title: Neurotoxicology
description: The effects of various harmful chemicals upon nervous system function. Emphasis given to the molecular events underlying neurological damage and to the relation of such processes to basic mechanisms of neurobiology.

title: Target Organ Toxicology I
description: Outlines vulnerability of selected organ systems to environmental and occupational chemicals. Reviews molecular aspects of toxicological damage. Topics include molecular toxicology and the following organ systems: nervous, cardiovascular, respiratory, dermal, and skeletal embryology.

title: Target Organ Toxicology II
description: Analyzes mechanistic responses in animals and humans to environmental and occupational chemicals and radiation, focusing on organ system physiology. Topics specifically covered include reproductive, endocrine, developmental, kidney, liver, pancreas, vascular, immune toxicology, radiation, and chemical carcinogenesis.

title: Experimental Design and Interpretation of Toxicology Studies
description: Introduction to methods of structuring toxicology experiments and analyzing data, including experimental design, data distributions, sample sizes, hypothesis testing, linear regression, analysis of variance, multiple comparison testing, and non-parametric tests.

title: Inhalation Toxicology
description: Explores laboratory inhalation toxicology principles and practices. Covers aerosols, gases, respiratory tract structure/function, lung defenses, exposure techniques, experimental designs, animal models, and regulations/guidelines.

title: Industrial Toxicology
description: Analysis of responsibilities toxicologists have in industry, including product safety, generating material safety, data sheets, animal testing, ecotoxicological testing, risk/hazard communication, and assisting industrial hygienists and occupational physicians; emphasis on interdisciplinary nature of industrial toxicology and communication skills.
prerequisites_raw: PUBHLTH 277B with a minimum grade of B- or EHS 206B with a minimum grade of B-

title: Introduction to Environmental Health Science
description: Explores environmental health's role in disease prevention. Studies human-environment interaction, focusing on chemical, physical, and biological agents in community and occupational settings. Covers climate change, environmental justice, children’s health, exposure assessment, and policy for public health improvement.

title: Air Pollution, Climate, and Health
description: Emission of air pollutants into the atmosphere, physical and meteorological processes that affect transport, and influence on global warming. Concepts of how and where people are most exposed, and how exposures and health effects differ in developed and developing regions.

title: Environmental Modeling and Risk Management
description: Learn general principles and basic mathematical methods for environmental modeling and human health risk assessment, including compartmental and advection-dispersion models for contaminants in air and water, uptake by plants and animals, exposure, assessment, dose-response modeling, risk management, and risk perception.

title: Independent Study in Environmental Toxicology
description: With consent from a faculty member who will supervise the program, a student may receive credit for individual study in some area of toxicology, culminating in the completion of a scholarly paper on the subject.

title: Health Psychology
description: Focus on theory and research in health psychology as applied to major acute, chronic, and occupational health problems. Adopting the biopsychosocial model of health, emphasis is on understanding and influencing how biology, behavior, and the environment influence health and illness.

title: Advanced Topics in Occupational Toxicology
description: Discussions with clinical and research faculty in environmental toxicology and occupational medicine on current toxicology problems in the workplace and critical review of current publications in the field.

title: Seminar in Environmental Health Sciences
description: Presentation and discussion of current research problems and issues by students, postdoctoral fellows, faculty, and guests, covering the broad research and policy areas of environmental health sciences.

title: Multicultural American Literature
description: Writings from at least two historically underrepresented groups in California and the United States with particular attention to historical conditions of literary production. Considers in-depth how literary works relate to racial constructions, economic conditions, and/or social movements.

title: Shakespeare
description: Plays by William Shakespeare are used to explore the playwright’s poetic gifts, theatrical imagination, and inquiry into human relationships and the human condition.

title: Topics in English and American Literature
description: Explores the diversity of human expression manifested in selected works of literature. By engaging with substantial literary texts, students will think critically about how meaning is created and how experience is interpreted in literary language.

title: Society, Law, and Literature
description: Examines how works of literature represent and influence the relation between law and society. The primary readings will be works of literature, but selections of works of law, politics, and sociology may also be assigned.

title: Society, Law, and Literature
description: Linked with Writing 60. Explores how works of literature represent and influence the relation between law and society. The primary readings are works of literature, but selections of works of law, politics, and sociology may also be assigned.

title: Young Adult Fiction
description: Traces the history and development of young adult (YA) fiction, with particular attention to the development of interpretive approaches to YA fiction that take into account YA fiction as a cultural phenomenon.

title: Introductory Seminar in English: Topics in Literary Studies
description: Discussion-based seminar on a faculty-chosen topic that introduces majors and those considering a major in English to interpretive methodologies and critical frameworks that characterize the field of English studies.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: The Craft of Poetry
description: Reading of selected texts to explore the ways in which these modes formulate experience. Students write several short analytic papers. Requires creative writing.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: The Craft of Fiction
description: Reading of selected texts to explore the ways in which these modes formulate experience. Students write several short analytic papers. Requires creative writing.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Sanctuary: Medieval and Modern
description: Principles and significance of the practice of legal sanctuary in medieval English history, literature, and religion. Development of modern use of churches and other safe spaces in the American Civil Rights movement, immigrant sanctuary movements, and international asylum.

title: What is a Person?
description: Contemporary debates about personhood in law, culture, and society. Beginning with the emergence of ideas of personhood in philosophy and theology, and culminating in the study of highly contested cases: slavery, abortion law, animal rights, corporate personhood, and artificial intelligence.

title: What is a University?
description: The history and present of the modern university, with special attention to the history of the UC system. Problems of social justice, racial equality, class mobility in the university as well as student life and universities in popular culture.

title: Introduction to Literary Theory
description: Using Plato and Aristotle as points of departure, addresses a range of perspectives and problems in literary theory. To be taken by English majors in the junior year.
prerequisites_raw: Three courses selected from ENGLISH 8 , ENGLISH 9 , ENGLISH 10 , ENGLISH 11 , ENGLISH 12 , ENGLISH 15 , ENGLISH 16 , ENGLISH 17 , LIT JRN 20 , LIT JRN 21

title: Undergraduate Seminar in Critical Writing: Topics in Literary History
description: Each instructor identifies a topic within literary history; special attention is given to mastering the conventions of academic argument and expression. To be taken as early as possible in the junior year.
prerequisites_raw: Three courses selected from ENGLISH 8 , ENGLISH 9 , ENGLISH 10 , ENGLISH 11 , ENGLISH 12 , ENGLISH 15 , ENGLISH 16 , ENGLISH 17 ; or LIT JRN 20 and LIT JRN 21 and one course selected from the above list. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Topics in Medieval and Renaissance Literature
description: Studies of works representative of Medieval and Renaissance literature in English, with attention to literary history, treating at a minimum more than one author and more than one genre.
prerequisites_raw: Three courses selected from ENGLISH 8 , ENGLISH 9 , ENGLISH 10 , ENGLISH 11 , ENGLISH 12 , ENGLISH 15 , ENGLISH 16 , ENGLISH 17 . Or LIT JRN 20 and LIT JRN 21 and one course selected from the above list

title: Topics in Restoration and 18th-Century Literature
description: Studies of works representative of Restoration and 18th-century literature in English, with attention to literary history, treating at a minimum more than one author and more than one genre.
prerequisites_raw: Three courses selected from ENGLISH 8 , ENGLISH 9 , ENGLISH 10 , ENGLISH 11 , ENGLISH 12 , ENGLISH 15 , ENGLISH 16 , ENGLISH 17 . Or LIT JRN 20 and LIT JRN 21 and one course selected from the above list

title: Topics in Romantic and 19th-Century Literature
description: Studies of works representative of Romantic and 19th-century literature in English, with attention to literary history, treating at a minimum more than one author and more than one genre.
prerequisites_raw: Three courses selected from ENGLISH 8 , ENGLISH 9 , ENGLISH 10 , ENGLISH 11 , ENGLISH 12 , ENGLISH 15 , ENGLISH 16 , ENGLISH 17 . Or LIT JRN 20 and LIT JRN 21 and one course selected from the above list

title: Topics in 20th-Century Literature
description: Studies of works representative of 20th-century literature in English, with attention to literary history, treating at a minimum more than one author and more than one genre.
prerequisites_raw: Three courses selected from ENGLISH 8 , ENGLISH 9 , ENGLISH 10 , ENGLISH 11 , ENGLISH 12 , ENGLISH 15 , ENGLISH 16 , ENGLISH 17 . Or LIT JRN 20 and LIT JRN 21 and one course selected from the above list

title: Topics in Literature, Theory, and Criticism
description: A series of lectures on and discussions of announced topics in literary criticism, theory, history, genres, modes, major authors.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Multicultural Topics in Literatures in English
description: Focuses on ethnic or minority literatures, or treats issues related to race and cultural identity.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Advanced Seminar: Topics in English Literature
description: Capstone course. Provides intensive work on a topic within the area of literatures in English with particular attention to the theoretical, critical, or conceptual issues it raises, with the goal of producing a substantive research paper.
prerequisites_raw: ( ENGLISH 101W or WRITING 101W ) and ( ENGLISH 100 and 102A ) or ( ENGLISH 100 and 102B ) or ( ENGLISH 100 and 102C ) or ( ENGLISH 100 and 102D ) or ( ENGLISH 102A and 102B ) or ( ENGLISH 102A and 102C ) or ( ENGLISH 102A and 102D ) or ( ENGLISH 102B and 102C ) or ( ENGLISH 102C and 102D ) or ( ENGLISH 103 and 102A ) or ( ENGLISH 103 and 102B ) or ( ENGLISH 103 and 102C ) or ( ENGLISH 103 and 102D ) or ( ENGLISH 105 and 102A ) or ( ENGLISH 105 and 102B ) or ( ENGLISH 105 and 102C ) or ( ENGLISH 105 and 102D ) or ( ENGLISH 100 and 103 ) or ( ENGLISH 103 and 105 ) or ( ENGLISH 100 and 105 )

title: English in Action
description: Career exploration for English majors connecting writing, close reading, critical analysis, and communication skills to diverse career paths including marketing, publishing, non-profits, technical writing, education, digital media. Special attention given to mentorship, job search strategies, resume writing, and interview techniques.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Topics in English Language Film and TV
description: Focuses on the analysis of film and/or television traditions in the English-speaking world, from a historical, theoretical, or comparative perspective.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Special Topics
description: Directed group study of selected topics as arranged by instructor.

title: Independent Study
description: To be taken only when the materials to be studied lie outside the normal run of departmental offerings, and when the student will have no formal chance to pursue the subject. Research paper required.

title: Master of English Seminar
description: Studies in selected areas of literary history for Master of English students. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Master of English Research and Writing Colloquium
description: Studies in selected areas. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Master of English Thesis Practicum
description: A yearlong undertaking of original research and writing, developed in close coordination with a faculty mentor. Accordingly, the precise contents and contours vary by advisor and by project.

title: Master of English Thesis Workshop
description: Students practice the scholarly genres that they will use throughout their career as an academic. The ultimate goal is to move toward a finished piece of writing: a masters thesis.

title: Studies in Literary History
description: Studies in selected areas of literary history. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Graduate Workshop in Academic Publishing
description: Reading and critique of student-authored essays with the goal of producing a publishable essay. Instructor leads discussion, meets with students individually, and provides an introduction to appropriate venues for publication and the process of submission, peer review, and revision.

title: Reading and Conference
description: Studies in selected areas. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Guided Reading Course
description: Studies in selected areas. Topics addressed vary each quarter.

title: Dissertation Research
description: A units-only course for students in the dissertation phase.

title: Rhetoric/Teaching of Composition
description: Readings, lectures, and internship designed to prepare graduate students to teach composition. Formal instruction in rhetoric and practical work in teaching methods and grading.

title: General Chemistry for Engineers
description: Emphasis on solid-state chemistry. Quantum theory, atomic structure, periodic trends, chemical bonding, molecular orbitals, electronic band structure, gases, liquids, intermolecular forces, unit cells, crystal lattices, phase transformations, and electrochemistry.
prerequisites_raw: AP Chemistry with a minimum score of 3 or SAT Subject Chemistry with a minimum score of 600 or SAT Mathematics with a minimum score of 600 or ACT Mathematics with a minimum score of 27. A score of 85 or higher on the Engineering Chemistry Placement Exam (fee required) is also accepted

title: Introduction to Engineering I
description: Introduction to engineering disciplines and the design process. Students enrolled in the online lecture also attend a three-hour lab on campus. Materials Fee

title: Introduction to Engineering II
description: Introduction to engineering disciplines and the design process. Students enrolled in the online lecture also attend a three-hour lab on campus. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ENGR 7A

title: Statics
description: Addition and resolution of forces, distributed forces, equivalent system of forces centroids, first moments, moments and products on inertia, equilibrium of rigid bodies, trusses, beams, cables.
prerequisites_raw: MATH 2D and PHYSICS 7C

title: Principles of Materials Science and Engineering
description: Superconductors to biodegradable polymers. Structure and properties of materials, including metal, ceramics, polymers, semiconductors, composites, traditional materials. Atomic structure, bonding, defects, phase equilibria, mechanical properties, electrical, optical and magnetic properties. Introduction to materials processing and synthesis. Materials Fee
prerequisites_raw: ( ENGR 1A or CHEM 1A or CHEM H2A) and PHYSICS 7C

title: Dynamics
description: Introduction to the kinematics and dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. The Newton-Euler, Work/Energy, and Impulse/Momentum methods are explored for ascertaining the dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. An engineering design problem using these fundamental principles is also undertaken.
prerequisites_raw: MATH 2D and PHYSICS 7C

title: Engineering and Computer Educational Laboratory
description: Comprehensive academic support designed primarily for underrepresented or underprepared students in Engineering, ICS, or selected areas of the physical sciences. Typical program activities: tutoring, study skills, career planning, self-esteem enhancement, library research techniques.

title: Public and Professional Service in Engineering
description: Student participation in public and professional service activities related to engineering.

title: Group Study
description: Group study of selected topics in engineering.

title: Special Topics in Fabrication Safety
description: Hands on training in the safe use of item fabrication: metalworking, woodworking, electronics fabrication, composites, welding, adhesives, water disposal, and others. Safety certification will be granted from this course and is required for access to Engineering School fabrication facilities.

title: Introduction to STEM Education Research
description: Introduces students to education research and topics studied in STEM education. Enables students to develop research questions, participate in research projects, design and utilize research tools, and contribute to STEM education research products.

title: Mechanics of Structures
description: Introduction to mechanics of materials. Topics include stresses and strains, axial and torsional loading, bending, shear, combined loading, stress and strain transformation, failure theories, beam deflection, and buckling.
prerequisites_raw: ( ENGRCEE 30 or ENGR 30 or ENGRMAE 30 ) and MATH 3A

title: Advanced Manufacturing
description: Principles in manufacturing processes. All machining requires energy: mechanical (cutting and shaping), heat energy (laser cutting), photochemical (photolithography), chemical energy (electro chemical machining and chemical vapor deposition). These methods and their fundamentals are examined. Materials Fee

title: Entrepreneurship for Scientists and Engineers
description: Learn the theory and practice of entrepreneurship and intrapreneurship. Covers positioning an idea, establishing the value propositions and benefits case, going to market strategy, creating an execution plan, and raising funds. Concepts are applied to a real-world venture project.

title: Senior Project - Topics Vary
description: Multidisciplinary group senior project of theoretical or applied nature involving design.

title: Communications in the Professional World
description: Upper-division technical writing course including the development of presentation skills. Effective communication with a range of audiences. Recognition of ethical and professional responsibilities for engineers.
prerequisites_raw: Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Curricular Practical Training
description: Practical training under an industry mentor in a technical field corresponding to students' area of interest.

title: Special Topics in Engineering
description: Studies in selected areas of Engineering. Topics addressed vary each quarter.
prerequisites_raw: Prerequisites vary

title: Engineering Thesis
description: Preparation of final presentation and paper describing individual research in Engineering completed in one or more quarters of individual study (i.e., ENGR 199 ).
prerequisites_raw: Completion of at least 4 units of Individual Research in Engineering. Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Honors Thesis
description: Preparation of final presentation and paper describing individual research in Engineering. For participants in the Campuswide Honors Program.
prerequisites_raw: ENGR H199 . Satisfactory completion of the Lower-Division Writing requirement

title: Individual Study
description: Supervised independent reading, research, or design for undergraduate Engineering majors. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.

title: Individual Study
description: Supervised independent reading, research, or design for undergraduate Engineering majors. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.

title: Individual Study for Honors Students
description: Supervised research in Engineering for participants in the Campuswide Honors Program. Students taking individual study for design credit are to submit a written paper to the instructor and to the Undergraduate Student Affairs Office in the School of Engineering.

title: Leadership I: Foundations and Innovation
description: Establishes a shared foundation in leadership, management, and innovation. Exposes students to a spectrum of leadership pathways, including intrapreneurship, product and engineering leadership, people and team management, and project and program execution.
